summary: Created a hardened systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 running as a dedicated unprivileged system user, confined to write only within /var/lib/inventory via ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths, with NoNewPrivileges=true and additional sandboxing (PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, capability/ambient-capability stripping, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, etc.). Verified the service is enabled and actively appending heartbeat/log data, confirmed a write attempt outside the allowed path is blocked (Permission denied), then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured boot_id baseline (83a0a80f...), issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until reconnection, confirmed a changed boot_id (d8a63ff9...) proving an actual restart, and verified the service came back enabled/active and resumed writing new heartbeat/log entries in /var/lib/inventory after boot.
actions_performed: Created system user inventory-worker (no login shell, no home)
Created /var/lib/inventory owned by inventory-worker with 750 perms
Installed /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh long-running loop writing heartbeat+log to /var/lib/inventory
Installed /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with NoNewPrivileges=true, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, and further sandboxing directives
Enabled and started the service, verified active status and confinement config via systemctl show
Verified sandboxing empirically: write attempt to /var/lib/test-escape.txt as inventory-worker user failed with Permission denied
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health baseline
Issued `systemctl reboot` on node1 via backgrounded sudo command so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed new boot_id differing from baseline, proving actual restart occurred

Verified post-restart: service enabled+active, ActiveEnterTimestamp near boot time, log file persisted with pre-restart entries and new post-restart entries appended (confirms both node persistence and continued healthy operation)

evidence.requirement: Service inventory-worker created, managed (systemd), long-running background worker
evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeds; is-enabled=enabled, is-active=active; worker producing tick=1 log entry and last-heartbeat file immediately after start

evidence.requirement: Confined to write only inside /var/lib/inventory, no new privileges
evidence.summary: systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, User=inventory-worker; empirical write attempt to /var/lib/test-escape.txt as the service user fails with Permission denied and file is never created, proving the sandbox is enforced not just configured

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service/data health) on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=83a0a80f-773c-4f3e-9137-1e7aa887b07a, service active/enabled, last-heartbeat and 1-line log present before reboot

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect; single node only
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `systemctl reboot` via sudo returned 'reboot command issued' with exit_code 0 before the node dropped off

evidence.requirement: Node actually restarted (changed boot identity, not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Connection timed out / reset while node was rebooting, then exec succeeded again with boot_id=d8a63ff9-a79a-44d3-af90-4a309cef60f3, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service, sandboxing, and data continuity
evidence.summary: After reboot: service is enabled/active with ActiveEnterTimestamp near boot time; sandbox properties (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths, User) unchanged; inventory.log shows pre-restart ticks 1-2 preserved plus new post-restart ticks 1-2 appended, and last-heartbeat timestamp advances during the wait, confirming the worker resumed writing to its confined directory after restart
